races.name: Barronstown Stud Irish European Breeders Fund (C & G) Maiden

runners_data.name: Bull Shark
runners_data.comment: Without a win yet, though he has shown the ability of a capable sprinter, he paid the price for being used too prominently in a Group 2 at Ascot last time, weakening out of contention well beaten. Sound surfaces suit, he is effective at 5-6f, and with more restraint today he could show a truer picture — his inability to convert remains the main concern.

runners_data.name: Darivan
runners_data.comment: By a high-class middle-distance performer out of a high-class middle-distance mare, this debutant has an attractive pedigree that suggests 7f and beyond will be within his compass in time. Jockey bookings indicate he is not the first choice from his yard today, so he is best treated with caution on debut.

runners_data.name: Giant Sequoia
runners_data.comment: Third on debut here despite being well supported — finishing below what the market expected but closing off encouragingly — he is bred for middle distances and the leading trainer-jockey combination keep faith. Experience from that first run should bring considerable improvement, and he is expected to be ahead of his mark before long.

runners_data.name: Oklahoma
runners_data.comment: Full-brother to a high-class performer who excelled over 8-11f, out of a multiple Group 1 winner over longer distances — this April foal carries outstanding breeding for middle-distance work. The trainer's record in this race is strong and he is no second-string stable entry; capable of a significant debut run.

runners_data.name: Shakespeare
runners_data.comment: A 1.3 million guinea Dubawi colt out of a top-class Group 1 winner at 8f, with a leading trainer and course handler behind him — the pedigree demands respect on debut. He is not clearly the first string from his yard today, which tempers expectations a little, but the talent is clearly there in abundance.

runners_data.name: Venetian Power
runners_data.comment: A St Mark's Basilica colt out of a smart dam who showed her best at 6-7f, with a half-brother useful over much longer distances suggesting varied scope in the pedigree. A top trainer and the betting market are worth watching — a debut runner with genuine interest though with plenty to prove in this company.

runners_data.name: Winnie's Wish
runners_data.comment: Below expectations in a maiden here most recently, a run that suggested the trip may have been insufficient, and he is yet to show his best in two outings. His breeding hints at longer trips suiting in time, and a step up in distance today may help — but he has plenty to find on current form.

runners_data.name: Yellow Sky
runners_data.comment: A Night Of Thunder colt priced at 140,000 euros at the sales, with a half-brother useful at 12f indicating middle-distance potential down the line. The trainer is in form, which is worth noting, but this debut presents a stiff task and he is one to monitor for future opportunities rather than back at this stage.

races.name: Airlie Stud Stakes (Fillies' Group 2)

runners_data.name: Confucius
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore-ridden O'Brien inmate with strong Good-ground form including a Curragh win; naturally wants to race prominently but is mapped to a hold-up position here given the field's prominent-heavy composition, so the style mismatch tempers how reliably it can deliver its best.|
runners_data.comment: Sixth but beaten less than two lengths in a Group 2 at Ascot last time, this imposing colt may still have been on the up. He handles both soft and fast ground at 5-6f; the leading trainer-jockey combination have a strong record in this race, and he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Dandyman Dan
runners_data.note: David Evans raider who is actually a front-running/prominent type by inclination, but with eight rivals pressing for those slots its natural position is unavailable; sim-going record is modest (0W0P) and 22 days off is not a concern, though the style displacement is the key check against it.|
runners_data.comment: Out of his depth over a longer trip at Epsom last time, beaten eight lengths on a stamina-testing track; back at 6f on a sound surface today he is firmly in his element. The trainer is in good form and he showed better ability before that defeat, but the class here still asks a question.

runners_data.name: Immortal Guard
runners_data.note: Two runs, two top-three finishes on Good ground at the Curragh — including a win — and Robson De Aguiar has found a lightly raced type who appears tailor-made for this trip; W J Lee sits in the prime tracking position and both sim-going runs have produced placing or better.|
runners_data.comment: Third in a Group 3 here last time, finishing with real purpose under pressure despite the defeat, he appeared to have more to give. Bred for and effective at 6f on this ground, he goes well at this track; the one question is whether he can translate that obvious promise into a winning performance.

runners_data.name: Mr Predicted
runners_data.note: Total unknown on style with no published form string, but Joseph Patrick O'Brien's 13/63 14-day record and Dylan Browne McMonagle in the saddle mean any ability will be maximised; the ⚠ lightly raced flag is genuine and this horse must be respected on potential alone.|
runners_data.comment: A $300,000 breeze-up purchase by the American sire Corniche, from a useful pedigree and with a top trainer's hand behind him — there is considerable interest here for a debut run. Fast ground should suit, and the market reaction will be informative, though debutants in this grade always face a stiff test.

runners_data.name: The Harv
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partnered this horse to a soft-ground win but form on Good (14th at the Curragh) creates a legitimate going question; sits at OR=120 which suggests the handicapper sees potential, and if the soft-ground win flattered, the Good rating here is the key watch point.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Ascot last time in a Group 2, finishing over nine lengths adrift when the level of competition proved too strong — that run reflects the standard he is being measured against rather than his true level. His debut was unremarkable and while improvement is expected, this remains a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Ballinea Star
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the field — her recent Curragh win over 6f on Good is directly relevant and she carries the lightest weight at 128lbs; Donagh O'Connor can bowl along uncontested, and the flat track removes any test of jumping away on an undulating surface that might expose her.|
runners_data.comment: Tough and willing when landing a maiden at Cork last time, digging in to hold on at the line by a short-margin — she has taken each run in her stride. Effective at 6f on good ground, she steps up in grade here, and with further progress still possible she is a credible danger to the top-rated.

races.paceDynamic: Ballinea Star is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only six runners on a flat 6½f Curragh track under Good ground, she is set to control proceedings from the front without meaningful pressure — a measured, sustainable gallop is the most likely outcome. Immortal Guard and The Harv are genuine prominent types who will look to sit just off the leader, while Confucius is a natural prominent racer redistributed to a hold-up role here because the field lacks true hold-up horses to fill that slot. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred positions; Immortal Guard and The Harv, both with clear form at this level, are best placed to actually hold the prominent berth directly behind Ballinea Star, while Confucius is racing out of its natural role. A controlled tempo from an uncontested leader on a flat track favours horses who can travel prominently and quicken through the race rather than those making up ground from off the pace — prominent-to-lead profiles hold the clearest positional advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ballinea Star Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Ballinea Star leads uncontested at a measured pace and quickens her own race from 2f out.
scenarios.body: If Ballinea Star leads uncontested at a measured pace and quickens her own race from 2f out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Picks Her Off
scenarios.trigger: If Immortal Guard or The Harv travel powerfully in Ballinea Star's slipstream and produce a sharper turn of foot in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Immortal Guard or The Harv travel powerfully in Ballinea Star's slipstream and produce a sharper turn of foot in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mr Predicted Announces Himself
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Predicted, lightly raced and unknown in style, travels with the pace and proves superior on raw ability.
scenarios.body: If Mr Predicted, lightly raced and unknown in style, travels with the pace and proves superior on raw ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong and the front runners tie up in the final 100 yards, opening the door for Confucius from behind.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely strong and the front runners tie up in the final 100 yards, opening the door for Confucius from behind.

watchPoints.text: Ballinea Star is entirely uncontested at the front — if she dictates a falsely slow tempo in the first 2f, the race becomes a sprint test from 2f out that will suit her sharp recent form over 6f at this track.

Immortal Guard and The Harv are both OR=120 prominent types who will contest the same tracking position directly behind the leader — watch for an early positional battle between the two that could force one wider or compromise its rhythm.
Mr Predicted has no public form record or known style; any significant market move before the off would be the primary intelligence signal that the O'Brien team has a serious runner on their hands.

Confucius is racing out of its natural prominent role and is being used to fill the hold-up position by redistribution — if the pace is slow and there is no true late kick to be had, its tactical displacement becomes an active disadvantage rather than a neutral factor.

The Harv's only Curragh run produced a 14th on Good ground, yet its winning form came on Soft — if the Good ground is riding on the faster end today, this is a material concern worth monitoring against its morning market price.

races.name: Neville Homes Summer Fillies Handicap (Premier Handicap)

runners_data.name: Fingerpaint
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who sets the pace; D K Weld handler, Colin Keane aboard, 20 days since last run — ran prominently out of role last time and that STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence she converts control into victory, though she shapes the race entirely.
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths in a Listed event at Navan last time, with her debut form since given added credibility; she has an attractive pedigree and first-time cheekpieces could spark some improvement. But her current mark looks stiff for a filly who has yet to make much impact in handicap company.

runners_data.name: Orchidaceae
runners_data.note: 287 days off the track is the key flag here; returned from a similarly long break to win a 7f Good ground race previously and her hold-up profile suits a scenario where the pace is genuine — A Oliver yard worth monitoring if fit signals are positive.
runners_data.comment: Absent for nearly ten months, she returns from a lengthy layoff after being out of form when last seen — well beaten at Leopardstown — and is just 1lb above her last winning mark. She is inconsistent and almost certainly needs this run, but if the break has rejuvenated her there is a mark to work from.

runners_data.name: Aviatrice
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has been placed four times on Good going without winning in those conditions; 13 days since last run and capable of tracking the pace from a forward position, but her 0W in similar going limits confidence.
runners_data.comment: Consistent and performing well until that Cork outing, where she went off too fast for the distance and emptied out in the closing stages; that run can be overlooked. She is generously treated on her all-weather form, handles 6-8f well, and a more restrained approach at a manageable trip should see a much better showing.

runners_data.name: Rion Rubette
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winner over 7f — including on Good ground at the Curragh — with Paddy Harnett claiming 5lbs; the trainer's strong 14-day record (2/3) and the horse's natural prominent style make this a serious contender in the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Progressive filly who landed a handicap at Gowran Park by a short-head last time, only getting to the line by a thread — the win came off a mark 6lb lower than today's. The new rating asks more and she will need to find further improvement, though her upward trajectory suggests she is not done progressing.

runners_data.name: Vega's Muse
runners_data.note: Two wins from eight starts on similar going and naturally races prominently; Shane Foley is a key booking but 41 days off the track and a flat recent sequence including a last-place run gives pause over current form.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten over a mile last time when her form fell away sharply, and even at her sharpest three starts back she needed a mark 9lb lower than today's. First-time cheekpieces are worth noting, but she faces significant questions and the current mark still looks too high on recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Greydreambeliever
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for the powerful Joseph O'Brien yard (13/63 over 14 days); holds up and has placed five times without winning on Good or Soft — a genuine contender if the pace scenario compresses the field late.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without converting — placed on several occasions in recent starts — she just failed to hold on at Gowran Park last time, going to the front earlier than ideal and caught on the post by a short-head off a mark 4lb below today's. Handles any ground over 6-8f, but is frustratingly prone to finding one too sharp.

runners_data.name: Nancy J
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been off 85 days; Ben Coen rides and her form includes a Curragh win, but the extended absence and a mixed recent record including a 13th on the Flat suggest she needs things to go right from the back.
runners_data.comment: Her return here was over an inadequate distance and she was below form, but stepping back up to today's longer trip — her best conditions — is the key angle, and with her trainer in fine current form she retains every chance off this mark. The ground suits and the break since last time is not a concern.

runners_data.name: Bint Majestic Roi
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, who saddles and rides, back-to-back winner over 6f on Good/Soft; a natural front-runner whose prominent instincts are squeezed back in this field — her recent wins came over shorter and the step to 7f combined with a compromised position is a compounding risk.
runners_data.comment: Won narrowly at Naas two starts ago, but her last outing over a longer trip resulted in a seventh-place finish well beaten — she clearly does not get beyond this sort of distance. Back at 6-8f today and 1lb below that recent run, though her official mark still looks tight for a horse in decent trim.

runners_data.name: Mallavelly
runners_data.note: Won over 1m on Good ground but has finished 7th twice recently, most recently 7/7f/SOF; Gary Carroll rides for G M Lyons (0/12 in 14 days), and while this horse wants to race forward, it has been edged to midfield in the mapping — the trainer's blank recent spell adds further caution.
runners_data.comment: Misfortune last time at Leopardstown saw her unable to get competitive off a slow gallop, leaving too much to do; that effort can be set aside. She handles any ground including today's and is at her best at 7-8f, with a first-time tongue-tie added; better conditions here should play to her strengths.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Natural forward-going type whose last three outings include a 7f Soft win and a 6f Handicap place; Wayne Lordan rides for M C Grassick (0/0 in 14 days) and no blinkered headgear noted, but this horse is better suited racing prominently — the redistribution back into midfield is a material disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Generally consistent over 5-7f, she was probably found out by a longer trip last time and beaten seven lengths; she is back at her preferred distance today and 2lb lower in the weights. First-time blinkers are new equipment, and her record — including a narrow win three starts back — suggests she can be competitive when conditions fall right.

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on a hat-trick bid following wins over 7f Good and 6f Good; OR of 86 reflects rapid rise and Chris Hayes continues on board for Denis Hogan (2/10 in 14 days) — a prominently-positioned horse whose current form is the strongest in the field and suits the dominant scenario directly.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last six starts in a sharp recent winning run, including a 2.25-length handicap success at Leopardstown off a mark 8lb lower — the handicapper has been busy, but her rate of progress suggests she may not yet be caught. Acts well on this ground over this trip; her upward curve makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: She's Too Kool
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who has placed twice at 7f on Good; Rory Cleary rides and Claire O'Connell sends her out 22 days after her last run — 0W in similar going and a moderate pace score (5/6 in similar conditions) means she needs conditions to conspire, but is not without each-way claims if the race develops late.
runners_data.comment: Highly tried at a better level earlier in her career and likely to have been exposed beyond her true level at that stage, she was beaten six lengths at Fairyhouse last time in modest company and has been without a win in recent starts. The effective trip is 6-7f, so conditions suit, but nothing in current form suggests a reversal here.

races.paceDynamic: Fingerpaint is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger pressing from the outside, she is likely to control tempo from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 7f at the Curragh. Behind her, Aviatrice, Rion Rubette, Vega's Muse, and Meriden will contest the prominent berths, creating a tight scrimmage for early position. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Bint Majestic Roi, Mallavelly, and Glory To Be are all genuine forward-going horses who will be squeezed back against their preference, with Meriden and Rion Rubette — both in sharp recent form — best placed to actually hold prominent ground given their handlers' intent and recent win sequences. A controlled, single-pace gallop set by Fingerpaint on flat, Good turf favours horses who can travel prominently and sustain a strong finish, making the prominent-to-mid profile the dominant winning profile, with genuine hold-up runners best served only if the pace accelerates sharply late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fingerpaint Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Fingerpaint sets an honest but uncontested pace and the race develops into a sustained 2f finish.
scenarios.body: If Fingerpaint sets an honest but uncontested pace and the race develops into a sustained 2f finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If Fingerpaint crawls and the whole field bunches, setting up a sprint finish that allows closers to sweep through.
scenarios.body: If Fingerpaint crawls and the whole field bunches, setting up a sprint finish that allows closers to sweep through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Scramble, Attrition Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of prominent types push forward aggressively early, elevating the pace and turning it into a test of stamina and resolution.
scenarios.body: If the pack of prominent types push forward aggressively early, elevating the pace and turning it into a test of stamina and resolution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Pays Off
scenarios.trigger: If one of the reshuffled prominent types — Bint Majestic Roi or Mallavelly — manages to recover position and produce a late surge from closer than expected.
scenarios.body: If one of the reshuffled prominent types — Bint Majestic Roi or Mallavelly — manages to recover position and produce a late surge from closer than expected.

watchPoints.text: Meriden and Rion Rubette are both on winning streaks and race prominently — watch whether Chris Hayes and Paddy Harnett contest the same pocket of cover behind Fingerpaint, as any traffic incident between them in the final 2f could decide the race.

Bint Majestic Roi and Mallavelly are genuine front-runners forced to race off their natural position — watch the first furlong to see whether either forces their way up regardless; if they do, the pace dynamic changes materially and the prominent scenario accelerates into an attrition test.

Orchidaceae returns after 287 days off the track — watch for market support and any pre-race signs of fitness; a fit reappearance from this hold-up type at 7f on Good ground could make her dangerous late, but cold form says treat with caution.

Greydreambeliever with Dylan Browne McMonagle is a consistent placer who has run 2nd twice at 7f on Good — watch where McMonagle positions her in the first half-mile; if he gets a clean run from midfield, she could be the chief beneficiary if the pace scenario favours closers.

Vega's Muse has been off 41 days and her last run was a 12th — watch her in the paddock and how Shane Foley positions her early, as she has the ability but needs to show she is back on terms before her prominent style becomes an asset.

races.name: Jebel Ali Racecourse And Stables Anglesey Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Beibhinn
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner off a 27-day break for Joseph O'Brien, won over this 6f/Good combination last time and goes well fresh; the key question is whether Declan McDonogh will fight for the rail against Ryan Moore on Sun Goddess or concede the lead and track.|
runners_data.comment: Winner at Listowel last time over this trip, building on a debut effort whose form has since been boosted at Group level — a strong signal her best is still ahead of her. She acts on this ground, and with further progression on the cards, she takes this step up in class on an upward curve.

runners_data.name: Belle Of The Ball
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Mrs Harrington with Shane Foley, drops back to 6f after a disappointing fifth at this trip last time but her sole win came over 5f on Soft so her effectiveness on Good at this distance is genuinely unproven; headgear (hood) adds a layer of uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Wearing a hood for the first time and drawn wide, she took a maiden at Cork by four lengths last time — dropped back in trip and ridden positively. The form of that win faces scrutiny, however, and she has a significant amount to find stepping up in grade against more proven opponents.

runners_data.name: Cleodolinda
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and unbeaten over 5f on Good ground for Donnacha O'Brien, now stepping up to 6f for the first time which is the critical unknown; Ryan's positive ride style could compensate for inexperience at the trip, and the form of both wins looks solid.|
runners_data.comment: Took a maiden at Navan last time — finding the stiff track to her advantage and winning by a length — and her debut form has since been given added credibility by subsequent runs. She acts on this ground and handles the trip, but this is a significant jump in class and she will need to find more.

runners_data.name: Controlla
runners_data.note: Very lightly raced, returned from a 14-length defeat to finish second over this 6f/Good trip last time out with Colin Keane, who knows how to ride a waiting race; trainer De Aguiar's 1/14 strike rate over 14 days is modest and the short 10-day turnaround merits a small flag.|
runners_data.comment: Green and below expectations at Ascot last time, beaten seven lengths in a Listed event, she clearly has more ability than that run suggests — her debut effort has been well franked since. Capable of better at 6f on this ground, but she is yet to translate her potential into results and has it to prove.

runners_data.name: Green Empress
runners_data.note: One run only — a second over 6f on Good — and Joseph O'Brien's yard is firing at 13/63; mapped toward the rear due to field redistribution but is a pace-committed type by nature and is unlikely to come from truly off the pace — McMonagle may prefer to sit handy rather than hunt cover.|
runners_data.comment: Showed promise on debut here — finding herself too far back to challenge but staying on to finish second, beaten five lengths — and that form has since been boosted by the winner at Group level. Acts on this ground and is expected to progress, though she is yet to score and faces a rise in class.

runners_data.name: Maggie Walker
runners_data.note: Won her sole start over 6f on Soft for David Marnane, an unknown quantity on Good ground and stepping into Group 3 company after a 39-day break; Luke McAteer's booking is workmanlike and the trainer's narrow book (1/9 over 14 days) gives little statistical anchor.|
runners_data.comment: Debut winner at Cork by two lengths in an auction race, she showed enough that day to suggest she has ability, but the form around that contest has not been strengthened and there is plenty to find when mixing with higher-quality rivals in this class.

runners_data.name: Sun Goddess
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore, Aidan O'Brien, and a 6f Good-ground win from last time — three strong positives — though she ran twice last week (8-day turnaround) and her OR of 103 is the lowest in the field, suggesting she may need the pace contest to set up rather than winning on pure class.|
runners_data.comment: Her run at Ascot eight days ago set the standard in this field — touched off by a length in a Group 3, well clear of those behind the front two — and the trainer has a strong record in this event. She acts on good ground and is right at home over this trip; the quick turnaround is the only caveat.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has slipped to 8th on her most recent start after back-to-back 5f wins; steps up to 6f and 10-day gap is tight, while P Twomey's 2/18 rate over 14 days is ordinary — the drop in form last time makes confidence difficult.|
runners_data.comment: Smart on her second start when taking a course-and-distance win, she was beaten four lengths in a Group 2 at Ascot last time on what may have proved an insufficient test — stepping back up to this trip, where she has shown her best, could unlock more. She acts on this ground and is well worth another chance.

races.paceDynamic: Beibhinn and Sun Goddess are the two confirmed front-runners in an eight-runner field, and with Ryan Moore aboard Sun Goddess for Aidan O'Brien, neither camp is likely to concede the lead without a fight — a genuinely contested pace is the default expectation over this 6f on Good ground at the Curragh. The early duel will set an honest, pressured gallop that compresses the field and limits the ability of either lead horse to coast in front and conserve energy for a kick. Green Empress, redistributed to a hold-up position, is naturally a pace-committed type rather than a true closer, so the field is actually heavier on forward-going runners than the map suggests — Beibhinn and Sun Goddess are most likely to secure the front two slots, with Maggie Walker and Belle Of The Ball the likeliest to press just off them. A truly run 6f on Good turf at the Curragh historically favours horses who sit prominent but controlled, just off a genuine pace, and can sustain their effort into the rising ground in the final furlong — the prominent-tracking profile is the primary beneficiary of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the Beibhinn–Sun Goddess duel produces a genuine honest gallop that burns off the leaders in the final furlong, rewarding the horse just behind.
scenarios.body: If the Beibhinn–Sun Goddess duel produces a genuine honest gallop that burns off the leaders in the final furlong, rewarding the horse just behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner gains a decisive early advantage and the duel is less intense than expected, allowing a clean lead with cover.
scenarios.body: If one front-runner gains a decisive early advantage and the duel is less intense than expected, allowing a clean lead with cover.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a truly scorching early tempo and tie each other up, opening the door for runners coming from further back.
scenarios.body: If the front-runners set a truly scorching early tempo and tie each other up, opening the door for runners coming from further back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Slowdown, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner pushes hard early and the race develops into a sprint from the 2f pole, suiting a pure turn-of-foot finisher.
scenarios.body: If neither front-runner pushes hard early and the race develops into a sprint from the 2f pole, suiting a pure turn-of-foot finisher.

watchPoints.text: Beibhinn and Sun Goddess — watch the early stalls break to see which jockey claims the rail and whether a genuine speed duel develops or one concedes immediately, as this defines the entire race shape.

Sun Goddess — Ryan Moore may use his tactical intelligence to manufacture a soft lead rather than fight, which would transform Scenario B from secondary to dominant; monitor her early stride pattern out of the gates.

Cleodolinda — watch how Gavin Ryan positions her stepping up to 6f for the first time; if she travels smoothly in third or fourth early it is a significant live signal, but if she is outpaced the trip extension is a real concern.

Green Empress — despite being mapped toward the rear, Dylan Browne McMonagle is an aggressive front-of-field rider and may push her up prominent early; if she appears in the first three on the home turn it changes the dynamic for the closers behind.

Velozee — a horse who has shown she needs things to fall right and whose last run was a poor eighth; worth watching whether W J Lee opts to cover her up and wait or push forward, as her positioning will indicate whether connections believe her best form is returning.

races.name: Paddy Power Pretty Polly Stakes (Fillies' And Mares' Group 1)

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Trainer De Aguiar has limited firepower at this level (T14: 1/14) and this 4yo's recent form (4th, 0th, 2nd on similar going) is patchy — she is a natural front-runner who, with the field crowded ahead of the pace, will be squeezed into a midfield role that does not suit her.
runners_data.comment: Improving but fragile when tested at this level; she was pressed too aggressively at Ascot last time and beaten six lengths in a Group 2, though she ran creditably in the circumstances. She handles any ground and this trip, but the top-class opposition here poses a stiffer test than she has faced before.

runners_data.name: Estrange
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 5yo has won three of her last five outings at 11-12f on similar ground and arrives 28 days fresh, making her the standout naturally-placed prominent type behind Thundering On — Daniel Tudhope's booking adds further confidence in a controlled pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in her last five starts seal her credentials, and her Group 3 success at Carlisle last month — asserting just enough off a slow pace — underlines her class at the top level. She holds something in reserve, handles any ground, and this trip sits comfortably within her range; hard to oppose.

runners_data.name: Nyra
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's 4yo has placed in five consecutive runs at 11-12f but is a front-running type who will be unable to assert her natural position in this traffic-heavy prominent group, likely settling deeper than ideal and reducing her winning prospects.
runners_data.comment: Placed at Group level in Germany and just caught at the line at Cork last time — when her rider lost the whip in a Group 3 — she is progressing with her new stable and has placed form that counts for something. Yet to win in recent starts, though, and this Group 1 field is a considerable step up.

runners_data.name: One Look
runners_data.note: Paul Twomey's 5yo has headgear flagged (p) and a consistent placing record at 10-12f on Good going, but the step back to 1m2f from recent shorter efforts and a T14 strike of 2/18 tempers expectations — tracks pace well enough to be dangerous for a placing.
runners_data.comment: Consistent at Group 2/3 level — fourth beaten two lengths over a mile here on her reappearance, stepping back up to this trip now in first-time cheekpieces. At her best she is a genuine Group performer, though she tends to find one or two too good and may again be outclassed in this company.

runners_data.name: Qilin Queen
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 4yo has winning form at 12f on Good going and is the most credible genuine hold-up type in the field, though her best wins have come on soft, and 37 days since her last run is a slight concern on fast ground — Shane Foley gives her a tactical edge.
runners_data.comment: Among the top performers in this division and generally dependable; her Group 1 run at Longchamp last time was over a trip shorter than her best, and being beaten eight lengths there can be set aside. She is at her element at 10-12f on any ground, and with course and distance form behind her, she is a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Red Letter
runners_data.note: Colin Lyons runs a 4yo who has placed six times in ten similar-going starts — she is in reality a prominent racer who has been redistributed to the rear of the field map due to pace overcrowding, meaning her natural finishing kick from a closer position may be compromised.
runners_data.comment: A filly who has shown real quality with notable regularity, stepping into Group 2 company at York last time and finishing a close second — beaten under a length — despite arriving at the start in a lathered state. She handles any ground and is effective at this trip; this step to the top level looks entirely warranted.

runners_data.name: Wemightakedlongway
runners_data.note: Wears a visor (v) and arrives on a 20-day turnaround for Joseph Patrick O'Brien, but recent form (4th, 3rd, 7th, 6th, 4th) is uninspiring and she is another natural prominent type unable to claim her role in a congested pace picture.
runners_data.comment: A former Group winner placed at Group 1 level, she has not recaptured last season's form in recent outings — outpaced over a less demanding track last time — and is yet to score this season. The visor is new equipment and a stiffer test may suit, but she has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Beautify
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore rides for Aidan O'Brien on this 3yo whose form line (6th, 8th, 8th, 2nd, 1st) shows a big drop in form at 7-8f on Good — steps up in trip and class here, and though she wants to be prominent, the crowded pace group will push her further back than Moore will want.
runners_data.comment: A filly who took a clear step forward when tackling a mile in a Group 1 here — closer to the pace than on previous starts — she is bred to progress further over middle distances. The ground suits, the trainer-jockey combination commands respect, but she is still building her profile and needs more at this level.

runners_data.name: Thundering On
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle's mount has won back-to-back including a 10f Curragh Listed win on Good and is the sole confirmed front-runner — the pace-setting role is hers alone, and on Good to Firm ground at this course she will be a hard horse to peg back if allowed to dictate cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Fresh from a dominant Group 1 win at Epsom three weeks ago — four lengths clear, picking up powerfully off a genuine gallop — she faces older fillies for the first time. Quick ground is untested, which is the one reservation, but her progressive profile and the manner of that success make her a formidable danger.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lace
runners_data.note: Listed as a non-runner — no tactical assessment applicable.

races.paceDynamic: Thundering On is the confirmed pace-setter and will lead from the front, with Joseph Patrick O'Brien's operation unlikely to restrain a horse who has won or placed prominently in all recent starts when allowed to roll along — on Good to Firm ground at Curragh over 1m2f, she will set a sustainable, metronomic tempo that is unlikely to be pressured into recklessness. Estrange, the highest-rated prominent type, sits naturally behind the pace and has an outstanding record in this going band (3 wins from 6 similar-going runs), making her the most naturally placed horse in the field to exploit a genuine but not suicidal gallop. The field is overloaded with prominent types — Beautify, Nyra, Carolina Jetstream, and Wemightakedlongway all want to race prominently but cannot all get their position, meaning several will be shuffled further back than is comfortable, compromising their natural rhythm and effectiveness. This race shape — a single front-runner setting honest fractions on fast ground with a clutter of displaced prominent types behind — strongly favours the closest genuine prominent racer tracking the pace, or a class hold-up horse who can pick them off late on a flat, undemanding track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Thundering On Leads, Estrange Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Thundering On sets a fair but manageable pace and Estrange travels smoothly in second or third, striking turning in.
scenarios.body: If Thundering On sets a fair but manageable pace and Estrange travels smoothly in second or third, striking turning in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady and Thundering On is never seriously pressured, enabling her to conserve enough to repel challengers.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely steady and Thundering On is never seriously pressured, enabling her to conserve enough to repel challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and a genuine hold-up type finds a clear run to pick off tiring leaders.
scenarios.body: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out and a genuine hold-up type finds a clear run to pick off tiring leaders.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Chaos, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the overloaded prominent group jostles for position early, creating a stop-start tempo that scrambles the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: If the overloaded prominent group jostles for position early, creating a stop-start tempo that scrambles the race shape entirely.

watchPoints.text: Estrange and Thundering On — if these two break cleanly and establish a one-two within the first furlong, the race is effectively run to a script that eliminates all of the displaced prominent types early.

Beautify (Ryan Moore) — watch the first two furlongs for Moore aggressively hunting a prominent position; if he commits early, it could force Carolina Jetstream and Nyra back further and create early crowding that scrambles the pace model.

Qilin Queen — Shane Foley will need a clear passage through the straight; if the displaced prominent types stack up ahead of her in the final two furlongs, her late run could be suffocated on this flat course.

Good to Firm ground confirmed for the 3:55 race specifically — horses with soft-ground form profiles (Qilin Queen, Wemightakedlongway) should be monitored in the market for any late drifts reflecting going concerns.

Venetian Lace is a confirmed non-runner — the field reduces to nine effective runners, which marginally eases the pace congestion behind Thundering On but does not fundamentally change the front-running dynamic.

races.name: Reserve Ladies Derby Handicap

runners_data.name: Touch The Moon
runners_data.note: Won over 1m4f on Good, has placed at 1m2f on Good; a confirmed front runner with a workable OR of 91, and 43 days between runs is not a concern with this trainer — but her claim depends entirely on being underpressed in front.
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent between codes, he most recently ran in a hurdle at Listowel where he went off too keenly and did not see out the trip; his Flat profile at 10-12f on a sound surface is the relevant form here. He has the distance and going handled, but the mark looks high enough for a dual-purpose performer with questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Clear Quartz
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with solid placed form at 1m on Soft but limited evidence on Good ground; the step up to 1m2f is worth noting given her recent runs have been shorter, though she presses up naturally and could benefit from a steady early pace.
runners_data.comment: Second beaten three-quarters of a length at Leopardstown last time on his return from a break — ridden positively at a shorter trip and performing well off today's mark. With plenty of scope still to tap into at middle distances, he arrives at 10f in his comfort zone with the going to suit; a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Musical Act
runners_data.note: Persistent hold-up type who has been finishing mid-field in all recent starts on Standard and Soft; the headgear visor may sharpen focus but her form string (74567) offers little encouragement without a stronger pace to run at.
runners_data.comment: Ex-Godolphin and Listed-placed in America, he has been finding his level in Irish handicap company and was clearly compromised by the soft ground at Leopardstown last time — today's sounder surface at 7-9f suits better. First-time visor is worth noting, but he remains without a win in recent starts and has plenty to do.

runners_data.name: Diamond Exchange
runners_data.note: Has won twice at around 1m2f on Good ground and shown consistent placing form at the trip — the strong trainer strike rate (T14: 5/34) and proven course-relevant form make her one of the more credible prominent movers in this field.
runners_data.comment: Unsuited by the drop back in trip last time and beaten fifteen lengths as a result — she clearly wants more ground, which she gets today over 10f. She landed a head-margin win at Leopardstown two starts ago off a mark 4lb lower, and first-time cheekpieces add interest, but the current rating may still be testing her ceiling.

runners_data.name: Fixation
runners_data.note: Ran second twice on Good ground over 8f and won over 1m2f on Standard; the headgear (p) suggests she needs a degree of organisation, and racing off a 35-day break for JP Murtagh's yard who have four runners on the card adds interest.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in his short career and ran his race at this track last time — performing creditably when stepped up in class and beaten five lengths. He handles 8-11f and first-time cheekpieces may sharpen him; the trainer is in good form, and he has shown enough in his recent outings to remain a competitive option here.

runners_data.name: Ob La Di
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who has placed on Good ground at 1m2f but has also posted 8th, 4th and strung together 12ths on Heap — her recent form is uninspiring and she will need genuine gallop to land a blow from the back.
runners_data.comment: Over-committed early at Gowran Park last time, unable to sustain the effort and well beaten; she has been hard to predict of late and has not managed a win in recent starts. She handles 10-12f and the ground suits her — the trainer is in decent form — but a more patient ride is needed for her to be effective here.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: Won twice over 1m2f and 1m on Standard and has previous Good-ground form; her true instinct is to race prominently but the congested prominent group means she is likely to find herself racing in a more restrained position than she wants, which tempers expectations under these conditions.
runners_data.comment: Yet to transfer his best form from all-weather to turf, and last time here he may have been found out by the distance, beaten seven and a half lengths; that run can be overlooked. First-time cheekpieces add interest, and if he can translate his artificial-surface ability to this surface he has the ability to play a part.

runners_data.name: Voice Of Reason
runners_data.note: Has placed twice over 1m4f on Standard with zero wins on Good in recent form; the low trainer strike rate (T14: 0/1) and lack of quick-ground evidence are mild flags, though she will travel naturally close to the pace.
runners_data.comment: His form on all-weather is far more convincing than his turf efforts, with his most recent grass run at Fairyhouse leaving plenty to prove on that surface. He handles the distance well on artificial ground, but two disappointing turf runs in succession cast genuine doubt about whether he can translate that form today.

runners_data.name: Earthwatch
runners_data.note: Returning from a 206-day break (22 days since a jumps run) and wears a tongue strap; the step back to Flat action is the key question, but her Flat form over marathon distances on Good ground suggests stamina is not the issue — fitness is.
runners_data.comment: Winner over a mile on the Flat with useful UK form, he has been erratic since and most recently competed over hurdles where he was put out of the race — a run to ignore entirely. First-time cheekpieces add interest, but he needs to find more to compete off his current mark on this surface.

runners_data.name: Great Mover
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with recent placed runs on Soft over shorter trips; she is naturally a prominent racer who is likely to end up racing in a mid-group position she is not entirely comfortable with, which the style-fit data (0.91) reflects — her best form has come under different tactical circumstances.
runners_data.comment: Second beaten three-quarters of a length at Leopardstown last time — well placed in a race controlled from the front, performing to her level off a mark 4lb lower than today. Effective over 7-10f and at home on this ground, she is without a win in recent starts but has a genuine chance if the race is run to suit.

runners_data.name: Senna's Girl
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue strap and has shown some minor placed form on Good ground at 8-10f; her hold-up style means she needs the pace to be genuine and sustained, and at OR 73 in this competitive amateur-rider heat she has ground to make up.
runners_data.comment: Given too much ground to make up at Gowran Park last time, she was beaten only 1.25 lengths from off the pace — closer to the winner than the margin suggests. She steps into 10f unexplored territory that should suit, and wears first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces; she rates the pick.

runners_data.name: Rocket Robyn
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 66 and her form includes a fade note; a true hold-up horse who has been pushed into a mapped midfield position, her recent form (29-806) does not suggest she can quicken sufficiently from off the pace even if conditions are right.
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight and a half lengths at Leopardstown last time when her stamina gave out at a longer trip — today's distance still looks the limit of her stamina. Without a win in recent starts, wearing a first-time tongue-tie, and with stamina questions to answer, she has a great deal to prove here.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Has the most mismatch between instinct and expected position — a natural front-running type who cannot get to the front in this race given the queue ahead of her; racing against her nature and at a low OR of 62, her redistribution to midfield is a significant tactical disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Third beaten five and a half lengths at Leopardstown last time, performing to his level at 9f — a distance slightly inside his best — and today's 10f provides a more suitable test. Without a win in recent starts but in fair trim, he has a chance here if he can build on that encouraging effort.

races.paceDynamic: Touch The Moon is the sole confirmed front runner and, with only one horse willing to lead, she will set a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f — a tempo that is unlikely to be aggressive enough to stretch the field early. Clear Quartz, Diamond Exchange, Fixation, and Voice Of Reason will press into prominent positions behind her, creating a compact, slowly-evolving race shape through the first half. The redistributed horses — Genoah, Great Mover, and Cooley's Mist — are true prominent types who cannot all claim the position they want; of those three, Genoah (who has won from the front at this course and distance) and Great Mover are most likely to push through and secure a tracking berth, while Cooley's Mist is likely to be shuffled back against her nature. A single uncontested pace-setter over an honest galloping trip on quick ground most reliably benefits horses who can track the leader efficiently and produce a sustained finish — prominent-to-mid-placed runners with proven form at 1m2f on Good or Good to Firm ground are the primary beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tracked Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Touch The Moon bowls along unchallenged and a close tracker pounces in the straight with a sustained finish.
scenarios.body: If Touch The Moon bowls along unchallenged and a close tracker pounces in the straight with a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely moderate and Touch The Moon or an early challenger simply is never headed.
scenarios.body: If the pace proves genuinely moderate and Touch The Moon or an early challenger simply is never headed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Run Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough that the early leaders stop, allowing a mid-race mover to sprint through gaps in the final quarter.
scenarios.body: If the pace is brisk enough that the early leaders stop, allowing a mid-race mover to sprint through gaps in the final quarter.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail To Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a sprint finish and hold-up horses, unable to close the gap, are left with too much to do.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses into a sprint finish and hold-up horses, unable to close the gap, are left with too much to do.

watchPoints.text: Touch The Moon sets sole front-running fractions — if she steals an uncontested lead and her rivals leave it too late to close, the race could be over before the straight begins; watch the early splits closely.

Genoah, Great Mover, and Cooley's Mist are all natural prominent racers and there is not enough room for all three to hold that position — watch for early-race jostling behind Touch The Moon that could unsettle all three.
Earthwatch has 206 days between her last Flat run and today; fitness is a legitimate concern and backers should watch her closely in the parade ring and at the start for any signs of rustiness.

JP Murtagh has two runners in the same race (Fixation and Ob La Di) — watch which one his stable jockeys appear more bullish about in the betting and pre-race demeanour, as one may be the stable's primary hope.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race specifically — significantly quicker than most of the card; horses with soft-ground form and no Good to Firm evidence (Clear Quartz, Musical Act, Senna's Girl) bear monitoring for any going concern in the market.

races.name: Fitzpatrick's Garage Group Handicap

runners_data.name: Valiant Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for De Aguiar who has struggled on Good ground recently (0 wins, 0 places from 4 similar-going runs), but 35 days fresh and drops to H which is his natural home; needs things to fall right late.|
runners_data.comment: A Dundalk specialist who has been well below his best in recent outings on turf, including a listless display in a Group 2 here — a run that suggests he is far from sharp on this surface. He handles sprint trips and is effective on artificial ground, but he needs to prove himself afresh on grass.

runners_data.name: Bishopton
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid course-and-distance form (placed twice at 6f on similar going), Lordan booked and trainer lightly raced over 14 days — one of the more likely to actually secure a prominent pitch given recent 6f STA form showing tactical versatility.|
runners_data.comment: In decent trim and narrowly successful at Dundalk off a slightly higher mark three starts ago, he was slightly outstayed when fifth beaten four lengths last time off a mark 1lb above today's. He handles the ground and is effective over this trip, but a career-best performance would be required to win here.

runners_data.name: Sommelier
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type with a tongue-tie, flagged for fading finishes; Harnett's 5lb claim helps offset the weight, but one win from 15 on similar going and a pattern of weakening late make this a tough sell in a strongly-run finish.|
runners_data.comment: A course winner here off a mark 11lb lower not long ago, he ran well enough at a lower level most recently and today's mark is only 4lb above that effort. New headgear in tongue-tie and blinkers; well treated on his best form and could still be competitive if that combination brings a positive response.

runners_data.name: Unauthorized
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 3yo with two wins already — including a 6f GOO victory — giving him solid credentials for today's conditions; Cleary takes the ride and this lightly-raced improver could prove better than his OR of 86 suggests if he gets a clean run from stall.|
runners_data.comment: Progressing with his new yard, he landed a 7f handicap at Listowel by over two lengths off a mark 7lb lower than today; the handicapper will have taken note. He handles the ground and is effective over this distance; further improvement is possible, but the new rating asks him to step forward once more.

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type at OR=78 who fades in finishes; seven wins and places from 15 on similar going shows course-and-distance competence, but he has not placed in six attempts this calendar year and is anchored at the back in a race that may not produce the late surge he needs.|
runners_data.comment: Former Group winner who has become unreliable, well beaten at Cork last time in a race that was over-ambitious in both class and distance. Today's 6f on good ground is closer to his best conditions, and he wears a first-time tongue-tie, but he has been without a win in recent starts and consistency is the issue.

runners_data.name: Flaming Rib
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator across 22 career runs who has been pushed into the midfield map due to surplus hold-up types; all five recent runs came at 7f on soft/standard ground, making this 6f Good assignment a dual concern on both trip and surface.|
runners_data.comment: Well treated on his best form in the UK, he put in a solid effort at Down Royal last time — beaten three lengths off a mark 3lb higher than today's — showing he retains ability. He handles any ground at 6-7f; the question is reliability, but on his best form he is competitive at this level.

runners_data.name: Inishfallen
runners_data.note: Naturally wants to be covered up and produced late — his two places from 15 on similar going came when granted that opportunity; shuffled into midfield on the map because the hold-up berths are overcrowded, and Colin Keane will have to manage the positioning carefully.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten eight lengths at Listowel last time without an apparent excuse, his recent Irish form has disappointed; he carries a modest strike rate in general. Yet his older UK form puts him on a mark that looks exploitable in theory, and first-time cheekpieces may trigger an improved response — not one to dismiss entirely.

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the powerful JP Murtagh yard, with a win and two places from 6 on Good ground; the 3yo is lightly raced, has place form at 7f on Good, and Rory Mulligan's 5lb claim adds appeal if the pace collapses to create a genuine late chance.|
runners_data.comment: A touch below form at Fairyhouse last time, beaten five lengths when stepping up in class, and without a win in recent starts. First-time cheekpieces may help and the trainer has been in decent form; today's conditions at 7f on good ground suit, but his current mark still demands more than he has lately shown.

runners_data.name: Nakamura
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 3yo from Murtagh's stable who has run well on Good ground (placed twice from 12 similar-going starts); blinkers on, McGettigan claims 5lb, and his ability to find prominent positions quickly makes him one of the more interesting plays if the early scramble creates a gap.|
runners_data.comment: Beaten only a half-length at Fairyhouse last time off a mark 1lb below today's — a close-run effort that keeps him firmly in the mix — and the trainer is in fine recent form. He handles the ground and trip, wears blinkers for the first time, and is worth including despite sitting 3lb above his last winning mark.

runners_data.name: The Piper's Call
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in a short three-run career with all three starts at 6f on Good ground — a profile that maps perfectly onto today; prominent style suits the expected shape, and Ben Coen's experience at the Curragh is a tangible asset in a congested field.|
runners_data.comment: Back from a 333-day layoff to win a maiden here by a neck last time, he heads into his handicap debut from a mark that looks fair, with 2yo form since boosted at Group level. He handles this ground at 6f; the wide draw at stall 16 is a neutral note, but on merit he looks the pick.

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer by preference but displaced to midfield on the map because this field cannot accommodate all seven prominent types; Adrian McGuinness sends him here after just 8 days, and the visor headgear is noted — but his true style is unlikely to be expressed unless the prominent scramble opens unexpectedly.|
runners_data.comment: A visor newcomer drawn wide, he ran decently last time when fifth beaten four lengths off a mark 1lb higher than today, and his best all-weather form puts him on a rating he could exploit. He handles the ground at various trips from 5-7f; a consecutive solid run could see him competitive off today's rating.

runners_data.name: Midnight Dusk
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner; his recent 1/6f/GOO win and back-to-back placed efforts at 6f underline why he commands this role, and an uncontested lead on Good ground over this flat 6f trip gives him every chance of lasting longer than a busier pace would allow.|
runners_data.comment: Back to form at Fairyhouse last time, narrowly winning a handicap when dropped in class and stepped up in trip — the combination clearly suited him. He remains on a competitive mark and handles a range of going at 5-6f; the yard appears to have him in a good place and he is a realistic contender.

runners_data.name: Real Encounter
runners_data.note: Prominent operator for Shane Foley and the Harrington yard, with Curragh 5f and 6f placed form on Good ground; three wins from 30 trainer starts over 14 days adds yard confidence, and his record of finishing first or second at 5f on Good (two occasions) shows he handles quick conditions well.|
runners_data.comment: Touched off by a neck here last time off a mark 4lb below today's, she came close and showed she handles course and distance well. Effective over 5-7f on this ground, her mark looks fair, and with a clear run she is a genuine threat despite carrying a small weight concession.

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: Prominent-leaning 3yo who steps up to 6f from a 5f campaign; Luke McAteer takes over and the Marnane yard has been quiet over 14 days — his best form has come at 5f and this step up adds an unproven dimension, though his 2/5f/GOO recent run shows he acts on this ground.|
runners_data.comment: Big and powerful, he showed he can handle turf at Cork last time when a 1.5-length second off a mark 6lb lower than today — an encouraging step. His best is at 5f, though, and the 6f trip here may not fully play to his strengths; he is one for a more suitable opportunity.

runners_data.name: Mary Shoelaces
runners_data.note: Natural prominent type who has been bumped into midfield because of the traffic volume ahead of her; Jessica O'Gorman's 7lb claim is significant given the 120lb impost, and two wins from 15 on similar going show she can run well on Good — but getting to her preferred position in a 17-runner sprint is the fundamental challenge.|
runners_data.comment: A multiple course winner here, she was comfortably held at Down Royal last time off a mark that is beginning to look above her current level; today's official rating asks the same question. She handles the ground at 5f and her course record is genuine, but this assignment looks too stiff for her current form.

runners_data.name: Joyful Tidings
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from Cromwell's in-form yard (4 wins from 42 over 14 days) who has one win and one place in nine similar-going runs; at OR=75 and 119lbs, the lightest weight in the field is the headline asset and a late run could be rewarded if the pace collapses through the final furlong.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth and a beaten 1.5 lengths at Fairyhouse last time when benefiting from a drop in class — he ran creditably off today's mark. He handles the ground at 5-6f and the rating looks fair; without a win in recent starts, but in fair trim, he is not without a chance in an open race like this.

runners_data.name: Heavenly Power
runners_data.note: Non-runner — no analysis applicable.|

races.paceDynamic: Midnight Dusk is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead in a race where seven others want prominent positions, she should find herself bowling along in front at a sustainable but not dawdling tempo on Good ground over 6f at the Curragh. Behind her, the prominent berths will be fiercely contested from the gate, with Bishopton, Unauthorized, Nakamura, The Piper's Call, Real Encounter, and Fox In Flight all seeking to settle in the first two or three lengths of the leader — a congested, potentially messy early scramble that will inevitably cost some of them ground and position between the 2f and 3f markers. Clonmacash and Mary Shoelaces are natural prominent types who are unlikely to secure their preferred pitch in this traffic and have been mapped to midfield accordingly, meaning their true tactical preferences will be frustrated from the outset. The race shape — a single front-runner setting a controlled pace with a wall of prominent horses just behind — classically rewards those who can travel close to the pace without burning energy in the early scramble and produce a sustained run from 2f out; horses with genuine prominent-to-held-up versatility and a clean passage are the profile that benefits most here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Midnight Dusk controls, prominent holds
scenarios.trigger: If Midnight Dusk bowls along uncontested and the pace is honest but not burning, allowing prominent horses to travel within themselves.
scenarios.body: If Midnight Dusk bowls along uncontested and the pace is honest but not burning, allowing prominent horses to travel within themselves.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, hold-ups swoop late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble burns out the pace horses and Midnight Dusk ties up inside the final 2f, creating a genuine late window.
scenarios.body: If the prominent scramble burns out the pace horses and Midnight Dusk ties up inside the final 2f, creating a genuine late window.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent scramble, chaos breaks
scenarios.trigger: If the seven prominent types collide in a badly-run race early, creating interference and shuffling positions through 3f out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed types find prominent spot
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly contracts and Clonmacash or Mary Shoelaces manage to secure their natural prominent pitch despite the congestion.
scenarios.body: If the pace unexpectedly contracts and Clonmacash or Mary Shoelaces manage to secure their natural prominent pitch despite the congestion.

watchPoints.text: Prominent scramble violence 2-3f out: with seven horses (Bishopton, Unauthorized, Nakamura, The Piper's Call, Real Encounter, Fox In Flight, Clonmacash) all pressing for the same three or four positions behind Midnight Dusk, check for bumping and checked runs in the early-to-middle stages — this is the highest single risk event in the race.

Midnight Dusk's stamina at 6f: her two wins have come at 5f and 6f on Good, but if the prominent horses push her fractionally quicker than she wants in the opening 2f, she may fail to last home — watch her stride length at the 2f pole.

Clonmacash and Mary Shoelaces position at start: both natural prominent types forced into midfield on the map — if either finds a clear run and slots prominently within the first furlong, their effectiveness improves materially and the scenario probabilities shift toward Scenario D.

The Piper's Call's unbeaten record at this course and distance on Good ground is the cleanest profile in the field — watch whether Ben Coen can slot him second or third without getting caught in the mass of prominent types immediately behind Midnight Dusk.

Joyful Tidings carries the lowest weight (119lbs) in the field for the in-form Cromwell operation — if the pace does collapse, monitor whether Chris Hayes can deliver him with a clear run down the wide outside in the final furlong.

races.name: Jo Browne Luxury Skincare Irish European Breeders Fund Maiden

runners_data.name: Banshof
runners_data.comment: Gave the impression on debut at Dundalk that the trip was too short — staying on late when beaten four lengths, suggesting more ground ahead could unlock improvement. His breeding also points to at least 7f; without a win yet, this step up into a maiden on turf represents the natural next test for him.

runners_data.name: Footstepstoglory
runners_data.comment: Beaten without being pressured at Limerick on his last run and showing signs of inexperience on that occasion, he remains green with plenty to prove; without a win yet, this looks a significant ask at this stage of his development.

runners_data.name: Forbidden
runners_data.comment: Well beaten on debut here and finding little when pressed — showing inexperience rather than outright lack of ability, but leaving everything to prove. A pedigree that speaks to speed at least offers a platform for future improvement, though she is hard to fancy on the basis of one uninspiring effort here.

runners_data.name: Mountain Memory
runners_data.comment: Eighth beaten eight lengths at Limerick last time after doing too much in the early stages — he ran to his level from that forward position. Bred for sprint distances, today's shorter trip may well prove more to his liking, and a more settled start could see him show his form in a better light.

runners_data.name: Saint Acclaim
runners_data.comment: A St Mark's Basilica gelding out of a smart dam who showed her best at 7f as a juvenile, with a half-brother useful over similar ground — the breeding profile is encouraging. The trainer is in form, a hood is fitted for the first time, and the market is worth watching on his debut.

runners_data.name: Spinola Bear
runners_data.comment: A Kodi Bear gelding acquired for 28,000 euros at the sales, with a half-brother useful at 7f and a dam who showed smart form at 8f in France — a pedigree with some sprint-to-middle-distance depth. The profile suggests he is worth watching rather than backing on debut, with plenty to prove in this company.

runners_data.name: Starborn Legend
runners_data.comment: Hampered and forced to switch on debut here, left with too much ground to make up when beaten 2.25 lengths — the circumstances excuse the result entirely. He acts on this ground at 6f, wears a tongue-tie for the first time, and with a clear passage his debut showed he is capable of winning soon.

runners_data.name: Suspicious Mindz
runners_data.comment: A useful maiden performer at his best who has become increasingly frustrating — well beaten at Fairyhouse last time on a sound surface without a clear excuse. He is effective at 7-8f and may benefit from first-time cheekpieces, but the pace of this race could find him out, and he is yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Tide Of Fortune
runners_data.comment: Runner-up on debut here, second by a neck after a slow start forced him into hard work early — he showed clear ability in difficult circumstances. Bred for 6-10f and acts on this ground; the wide draw at stall 19 is the practical concern, but there is clear improvement to come and he is a genuine danger.

runners_data.name: Trek Home
runners_data.comment: Showed clear progression from his debut when fourth beaten two lengths here last time, despite doing too much in the early stages — the experience is clearly doing him good. By a Group 2 sprint winner and effective at 5-6f, he can continue to hold his own in this class as he learns to settle.

runners_data.name: Amerilis
runners_data.comment: Second beaten 3.5 lengths in a handicap here last time when dropped in class — she ran to her level and is in decent form heading into this. Effective at 6f with cut in the ground, she adds a tongue-tie for the first time; yet to score in recent starts, but her form means she is not without a chance.

runners_data.name: Cara Teaghlaigh
runners_data.comment: A Profitable filly acquired for 5,500 euros at the sales, drawn wide in a 21-runner field and from a yard that has had a quiet season. With an unraced dam and no form to call on, she is very much one to observe rather than support at this stage.

runners_data.name: Dandymaria
runners_data.comment: Fourth on debut at Down Royal, beaten over six lengths but leaving a promising impression — the debut clearly showed more than the finishing position conveys given her inexperience. Bred for sprint distances around 6f with improvement expected from that first run, she is a genuine danger if she settles; the wide draw is the practical concern.

runners_data.name: Focaccia
runners_data.comment: Showed her hand on handicap debut here, running well below expectations and flashing her tail — behaviour that suggests she can be reluctant when asked. She has shown ability previously but is best over 5f mainly on all-weather; she needs to iron out her attitude before becoming reliable, and a repeat of that performance is the concern.

runners_data.name: Forza Magico
runners_data.comment: An Aclaim filly, full-sister to a very useful juvenile at 7f and out of a smart dam at 8f — a family with genuine early speed. The yard has a strong record in this race, but on a debut with no known form this looks a learning exercise rather than a realistic winning opportunity.

runners_data.name: Hazrama
runners_data.comment: Back after a ten-month absence, her only run on debut at Naas left plenty to prove — beaten seven and a quarter lengths. Drawn near the inside of a large field, which is a mild positive, but she remains a work in progress and will need significant improvement from that debut performance.

runners_data.name: Lady Moon
runners_data.comment: Ninth and well beaten in her only start here, she clearly has plenty of ground to make up to become competitive. A pedigree mixing speed and stamina offers scope for different trips, and a first-time tongue-tie is worth noting; drawn near the rail in a big field, but significant improvement on what she has shown is required.

runners_data.name: Leannespour
runners_data.comment: Back after a nine-month absence, she was well beaten in her last run here without getting near the pace — a run that already factored in inexperience. Drawn wide in a big field and without a win from either start, she is clearly still developing; speed in her pedigree suggests the distance is right, but a significant turnaround is needed.

runners_data.name: Lilli's Angel
runners_data.comment: A Sioux Nation filly out of a dam who excelled at 6f and showed her best on her second start — a family background that offers cautious encouragement. Her yard is capable of having debutants well-prepared and the market is worth monitoring, but beyond that there is no form to assess and she is a speculative interest.

runners_data.name: Off We Go
runners_data.comment: A Cotai Glory filly acquired for 7,500 euros at the sales, half-sister to a useful juvenile at 7f — a pedigree that suggests early pace. Drawn near the inside of a 21-runner field, but this is a tough task on debut and she is one to follow once she gains experience rather than act upon immediately.

runners_data.name: Solana Beach
runners_data.comment: Third beaten 2.25 lengths at Gowran Park last time in a handicap at a shorter trip — she performed consistently to her level and retains good form. Effective at 7f-1m on this ground, she has a genuine chance in this maiden if her short-career consistency translates here, and a step back up to a suitable trip is the key angle.
